messages:
monitor-bot: :warning: Alert from cluster-monitoring: conntrack usage > 95% on 6/12 nodes in us-east-1 gpu-pool. ~1.2k pod connections dropped in the last 5m. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/conntrack/conntrack-overview

alexa: fyi seeing p99 spike on east-west RPCs, looks like a bunch of retries. likely related to that alert.

sam: can someone paste the conntrack counts from an affected node? run `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` and `conntrack -L | wc -l`

jia: grabbed one node (gpu-az1-004) right now:```
# sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count
3276800
# sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
33554432
# conntrack -L | wc -l
3276800
```

marta: whoa that's pretty close to the max. are we sure this is conntrack growth and not ephemeral port exhaustion or something leaking from kube-proxy? I'm seeing a lot of MASQUERADE hits on those nodes.

ryan: we rolled a kernel bump (5.15 -> 6.1) on that pool two nights ago and flipped a couple netfilter flags in the build. possible GC behavior changed for conntrack. also check `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established`.

alexa: also observed many entries stuck in TIME_WAIT and some ESTABLISHED for pods that no longer exist — suggests conntrack entries aren't being GC'd quickly.

sam: immediate mitigations I recommend: 1) bump `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` by ~2x on affected nodes via a privileged DaemonSet, 2) reduce `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` from 432000 to 600 (temporary), 3) monitor `conntrack -L | awk '{print $NF}' | sort | uniq -c` to see state distribution. Longer term: tune kube-proxy conntrack settings or move to ipvs mode and review `noMasquerade` for intra-cluster pod-to-pod traffic.

jia: applied a quick job to set `nf_conntrack_max=67108864` and `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=600` on 6 nodes (gpu-az1-00[3-8]) — rolled as privileged DaemonSet; logs here: https://logs.redwood.internal/conntrack-patch/1741204321

monitor-bot: :white_check_mark: After patch: gpu-az1-004 nf_conntrack_count -> 2,110,432 (down from 3,276,800). Dropped connection rate also declined.

marta: good. we'll need a follow-up to update our bootstrapping / node config so this persists and to add a safe guard in cluster-autoscaler profile for this pool. also open question: can we avoid SNAT for east-west pod traffic to reduce conntrack pressure?

ryan: you can reduce SNAT by using kube-proxy with proper `--cluster-cidr` / `--masquerade-all=false` and supporting routes, but cross-node pod-to-pod may still create conntrack entries depending on CNI. we'll test on staging.

alexa: created ticket https://go/repo/infra/conntrack-eastwest-2026 assigned to eng-net, adding playbook steps and runbook. :memo:

sam: action items:
- [ ] add alert: nf_conntrack_count > 85% for 10m
- [ ] audit recent kernel/netfilter changes on gpu-pool rolling update
- [ ] test ipvs + conntrack timeout changes in staging and measure p99 latencies

jia: attached conntrack dumps and a short grep for leaking source IPs to the ticket. pinging @oncall for regressions.

marta: leaving note — we'll consider conntrackd or hashsize tuning if GC isn't keeping up. thanks team. :thumbsup:

alexa: :eyes: monitoring dashboard will be updated with the new alert thresholds and a dashboard panel for conntrack timeouts.

sam: closing the immediate incident for now but keeping the ticket open for follow-ups.

monitor-bot: :rocket: Incident window: 2026-03-04T02:52:01Z -> 2026-03-04T03:07:00Z — follow-ups tracked in https://go/repo/infra/conntrack-eastwest-2026
